VR Training

Prismo

Prismo ("Tu vois ce que je vois", do you see what I see) makes people want to work in care jobs by letting them live a moment of the job in VR. In the scenarios, the player stands inside a 360° video filmed on site, such as a heart massage or a computer repair workshop: the video stops on questions, and the player spots the dangers around them with a flashlight. The impairment simulator is a game for two or a whole class: the player in the headset sees a broken music box only through a small lens, while the others read the printed repair notebook and talk them through it, with no impairment or with colour blindness, tunnel vision, a central blind spot or dyslexia. Trainers create and edit scenarios inside the headset, with no new build. Two bonuses, a spinning vortex tunnel and a plank over a 220 m drop, break the ice. Runs fully offline on Meta Quest 2 and 3, with controllers or bare hands, and anyone on the same network can follow the player's view in a browser.

Features

  • 360° video that stops on questions, with an explanation and a retry after a wrong answer
  • Flashlight hunt for the dangers in each scene, and info points to open
  • Impairment simulator: a broken music box, repaired by talking, seen through a small lens
  • No impairment, colour blindness, tunnel vision, central blind spot or dyslexia
  • Printed repair notebooks in three levels; in class the pages are split between tables
  • In-headset workshop to create and edit scenarios, with no new build
  • Two bonuses: a vortex tunnel and a plank over a 220 m drop
  • Live view of the headset in any browser on the same network
  • Controllers or bare hands, fully offline on Quest 2 and Quest 3
